newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk rights group says Kurds forced to bear arms.
newsitem.headline: Turk rights group says Kurds forced to bear arms.

text.p: Turkish human rights officials said on Friday that security forces had threatened to raze a Kurdish town and kill its inhabitants if they did not join an anti-rebel militia.

A high-ranking Turkish security official said reports of the alleged incident in the southeastern town of Lice had been blown out of proportion. "All the statements made were exaggerated," he told Reuters.
The Human Rights Association (IHD) said in a statement: "They made it clear that Lice had to accept the village guard system or they would kill everyone, including children, and burn Lice."

The IHD said gendarmerie troops gathered some 2,000 males aged between 15 and 70 in Lice on December 20 and told them they needed 100 people to become members of the state-paid militia, which fights Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels.
It said seven people were beaten with weapons after nobody from the crowd had offered to join the militia in an all-night ordeal.
Turkey is under pressure from Europe for rights abuses, many of which are alleged to occur in the southeast where troops have been battling the guerrillas for 12 years.
More than 21,000 people have died in the conflict.
The rights group said 110 people were detained for a further two days and later sent home with guns. The security official said the Kurds had taken up arms of their own free will.
"Lice is a sensitive area...some of the people accepted joining the militia, some did not," he said. "(The guards system) is an important source of revenue for people," he said.
More than 60,000 men, mostly Kurds, are members of the militia.
